headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear a greater share of the costs for grid infrastructure, reducing the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Consumer advocates, residential ratepayers, environmental groups, Senator L. Louise Lucas, U.S. Sen. Mark Warner.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Warner Backs Bill to Shift Data Center Costs Away from Ratepayers
news_summary: U.S. Sen. Mark Warner has co-sponsored legislation, the Power for the People Act, aimed at making data center operators pay more for their significant energy demands and associated infrastructure upgrades. Supporters argue that data centers currently increase consumer costs through higher electricity demand and grid expansion expenses, which are often passed on to all utility customers.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This legislation requires water utilities to report monthly water consumption data for data centers, enhancing transparency on their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local governments, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (potentially, due to increased regulatory burden and disclosure of previously private data).
news_headline: Virginia to Require More Detailed Water Use Reporting for Data Centers Beginning in 2027
news_summary: Virginia has approved legislation, identical to SB 553, that will mandate water utilities to provide detailed monthly reports on water usage by data centers and other major customer categories, effective January 1, 2027. This move aims to improve transparency and inform future discussions on infrastructure planning and water resource management amidst rapid data center growth.

headline: Establish Data Center Siting, Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill requires new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to conduct site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools, and allows localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Delegate Thomas, Senator Roem.
opponents: Data center industry, developers (due to potential restrictions and increased assessment requirements).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data centers to assess noise, environmental impacts
news_summary: Virginia's HB 153, which has passed, mandates that new high energy use facilities, such as data centers, conduct site assessments to examine their sound profiles on nearby homes and schools. The legislation also empowers localities to require assessments of potential impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources, providing a foundation for stronger future regulations.
